title: CAD/BIM exact-version licensing/composition evidence (web + Electron/desktop)
objective: Produce exact-version licensing/composition EVIDENCE for the CAD/BIM stack actually tested across RESEARCH-CAD-001..005 (IfcOpenShell 0.8.5, OCCT 7.8.1 via cadquery-ocp 7.8.1.1.post1, cadquery 2.6.1, ezdxf 1.4.3, numpy 2.1.3, FreeCAD 1.1.3 AppImage, Python 3.12.13), covering BOTH the web deployment model and the Electron/desktop deployment model. Record each component's exact version from the authoritative pinned sources, identify each license from stable upstream facts, raise composition flags for the LICENSE-001 gate, and analyse both deployment models' LGPL posture. This gate does NOT approve any composition, does NOT change production packaging, and does NOT alter Architecture v1.1; it produces the inventory and flags that feed LICENSE-001's legal/architect review.
acceptance_criteria: The exact version of every tested component is recorded from the authoritative pinned sources (CAD-001 requirements.txt, the CAD-001..005 committed environment.json snapshots, and the FreeCAD AppImage SHA256 manifest), cross-checked against the currently-importable distribution metadata where present.
Every tested component's license is identified from a stable upstream statement and SPDX-classified (copyleft vs permissive).
A composition flag matrix is complete: every component carries an explicit flag and severity for the LICENSE-001 review; no composition is approved by this gate (the decision owner is LICENSE-001).

The web deployment model is analysed: the tested server-side path is documented, the WASM/in-browser-native path is explicitly recorded as not tested, and the LGPL posture (pure SaaS vs distributable web client) is documented.

The Electron/desktop deployment model is analysed: the tested native-worker path is documented, the Electron host license is recorded, and the LGPL posture (dynamic/separate-process linking + written offer for source; no static linking of LGPL into closed-source code) is documented.

The frozen adapter boundary (Architecture v1.1) is identified as the LGPL-compliance mechanism that preserves the user-replacement right for every copyleft component in both deployment models, referencing the RESEARCH-CAD-001 item-9 adapter-replacement proof.

The evidence identifies the central composition fact: no GPL (strong copyleft) component is present in the tested stack (all copyleft present is LGPL), so no GPL-contamination path exists from the CAD/BIM stack into a closed-source composition.
Results support, reject, or defer the licensing/composition posture under the frozen architecture (recommendation only; LICENSE-001 decides).
non_goals: No legal/composition approval (that is LICENSE-001's decision).
No production packaging change (out of scope per Issue #6).
No architecture change (Architecture v1.1 remains FROZEN).
No re-measurement of CAD/BIM performance or capability (those are CAD-001..005's evidence; this gate is a records/inventory benchmark).
No final adapter-boundary + replacement-path + end-to-end-workflow proof (that is RESEARCH-CAD-007's scope, per the Issue #6 directive).
risk_assumptions: POST-MERGE VERIFICATION COMPLETED: RESEARCH-CAD-001..005 dependencies are VERIFIED. RESEARCH-CAD-006 was merged into main at 74f95529f20a0840f6e1189a37e3b9a3d9c8c34f. The post-merge governance run 32997108160 (#67) and research-cad-006 run 32997108095 (#3) both completed successfully on that exact merge revision. The dependency invariant was satisfied without weakening the validator.

SPEC DIVERGENCE: spec/work-items.md still carries the older RESEARCH-CAD-006 definition ('CAD/BIM performance and file-size gate', dependencies RESEARCH-CAD-001 only). Per the Issue #6 execution directive, the authoritative scope is exact-version licensing/composition evidence covering web + Electron/desktop deployment models (same superseded-wording pattern as RESEARCH-CAD-001..005, where the GitHub Issue redefines the work item and the implementer follows the Issue, flagging the divergence). This record follows Issue #6.

Architecture version: this record targets v1.1 (active, FROZEN) per the execution directive ('Architecture: v1.1 frozen'). The spec/work-items.md 'Architecture version: 1.0' header predates the ACR-002 merge (same superseded-wording situation recorded in RESEARCH-CAD-003/004/005).

Records/inventory only: this gate does not exercise the CAD/BIM engines; versions are asserted from the committed authoritative pinned sources (CAD-001 requirements.txt + the CAD-001..005 environment.json snapshots + the FreeCAD AppImage SHA256 manifest), cross-checked against the currently-importable distribution metadata where present. Non-importable distributions in a given evidence-collection environment (e.g. ifcopenshell, FreeCAD AppImage) are recorded honestly from the pinned sources, not coerced.

WASM not tested: the web model's in-browser-WASM path (OCCT emscripten, cadquery-ocp WASM, IfcOpenShell WASM) was not exercised in CAD-001..005; the tested web path is server-side only. A distributable web client bundling LGPL WASM would need LICENSE-001 Section 4 review (flagged, not approved).

Final-proof scope boundary: the final adapter-boundary + replacement-path + existential end-to-end-workflow proof is RESEARCH-CAD-007's scope (the final CAD/BIM feasibility gate, per the Issue #6 directive). This gate references CAD-001's existing replacement proof as the basis for the LGPL-compliance analysis; it does not re-prove the replacement path end-to-end.
evidence_requirements: Exact versions of every tested component recorded from the authoritative pinned sources, cross-checked against currently-importable distribution metadata where present.
Licenses identified from stable upstream statements and SPDX-classified.
Composition flag matrix complete (every component carries an explicit flag and severity); no composition approved.
Both deployment models (web + Electron/desktop) analysed with documented LGPL posture.
The adapter boundary (Architecture v1.1) identified as the LGPL-compliance mechanism, referencing the CAD-001 item-9 replacement proof.
Records/inventory benchmark reproducible from the committed pinned sources (no CAD engine exercise required).
